question: Does the second stream change the answer?
what_it_does: Refit every species with iNaturalist removed; compare the trend
finding: Run on 26 of 34 species on the full record; superseded for reporting by the five-year version above

question: Do the streams agree spatially?
what_it_does: Exponent linking records to camera abundance, with both thresholds
finding: On the full-record fleet 2 of 25 intervals include 0 and 5 reach 1; median theta1 0.56

question: Does that agreement hold over time?
what_it_does: Coupling re-estimated per year, 2019-2025, plus its spatial driver
finding: Drift runs in both directions across 23 species, median +0.019 per year, so no uniform time trend in the coupling

question: Does the study-area definition matter?
what_it_does: IUCN polygon vs presence threshold vs union, on records and fitted cells
finding: Compared on 3 species; the union mask was adopted

question: Does the spatial parameterisation matter?
what_it_does: Same bundle, scalar vs region-varying trend; interval width and resolution
finding: Compared on 3 rows; the ecoregion fit carries a localised spatial-field convergence failure the national fit does not

question: Does the camera likelihood matter?
what_it_does: Same deer bundle, detection/non-detection vs negative binomial counts
finding: Same deer bundle both ways: occupancy +4.08%/yr, counts +3.46%/yr, so discarding count information biases the trend upward by about 15%

question: Is occupancy saturating?
what_it_does: Fitted psi distribution and implied per-site abundance from the fitted models
finding: Examined for 3 species; deer is the saturating case at 79% of deployments and median fitted psi 0.952

question: Is occupancy saturating?
what_it_does: Naive occupancy and implied animals per site from raw detections; no fitted psi
finding: Screened 34 species from raw detections to decide which needed a count-based camera arm

question: Is the estimator choice defensible?
what_it_does: Bias, coverage and detection rate across estimator arms and abundance levels
finding: Superseded by the power and data-volume rows below, which use the corrected null and the abundance ladder

question: Do independent data agree?
what_it_does: Model direction against state agency trend assessments
finding: Of 34 species, 5 agree and 1 differ with the published agency direction

question: Is agency agreement window-sensitive?
what_it_does: 5-year vs 10-year agency windows scored separately
finding: Re-scoring on the ten-year window traded one disagreement for several, so the five-year scoring stands

question: Are the camera inputs faithful?
what_it_does: Model-input detecting deployments against the raw sequence files
finding: Model-input detecting deployments reconciled against the raw sequence files for 25 species

question: Is camera effort stationary?
what_it_does: Share of cells sampled only early or only late in the record
finding: Computed for 25 species; see the table for per-species shares

question: Are degenerate records excluded?
what_it_does: Deployments with zero or missing survey nights, by species mask
finding: 104 deployments have zero or missing survey nights, across 16 projects

question: Did the chains converge?
what_it_does: R-hat by parameter family, single-shot runs
finding: On the five-year fleet the trend family converged for 14 of 15 species; the only failure is collared peccary

question: Where is anchoring weakest?
what_it_does: Camera-only displacement against range size and camera coverage
finding: Displacement from the camera-only fit tracks range size (Spearman -0.61, p=0.005); the three failures all occupy fewer than 100 cells

question: Do urban and rural trends differ?
what_it_does: year_pop interaction on the iNaturalist stream, tier-2 fits
finding: Not run on the five-year window

what_it_does: cam_dev random field added to the camera submodel
finding: Moved western gray squirrel from -13.2 to -1.4%/yr, close to its camera-only -2.7; not yet tested on the other two failures

question: Do projects differ systematically?
what_it_does: Project-level intercept on the camera detection model
finding: Not run

question: Does the second stream change the answer?
what_it_does: Refit every species with iNaturalist removed; compare direction and magnitude
finding: 13 of 15 joint estimates fall inside the camera-only interval; coyote and California ground squirrel fall outside

question: Do the streams agree spatially?
what_it_does: theta1 band, camera-only verdict match, and whether cameras alone support the number
finding: 5 of 15 pass all three; 13 pass the verdict check and 13 the containment check

question: Why does theta1 sometimes fail?
what_it_does: Chain spread in within-chain SDs against surface contrast and camera volume
finding: Six species mix slowly, three settle in different places; both contrast and camera volume matter jointly, neither alone

question: Does the trend window matter?
what_it_does: Same species and model fitted on five-year, ten-year and full-record windows
finding: Deer runs +4.0%/yr on the full record, +0.46 over ten years and -0.73 over five

question: Do reporting campaigns bias the records?
what_it_does: Difference-in-differences on target species' record share inside campaign footprints
finding: Campaigns shifted reporting toward their target without recruiting observers, so the effect is selectivity rather than effort

question: Can campaign effects be modelled?
what_it_does: Graded cell-level exposure from county footprints, with tightened spatial bounds
finding: Estimates are confounded with real local abundance change, so they are reported as a limitation and not used as priors

question: Do domestic animals distort effort?
what_it_does: Observer profiles and the cell-year effort denominator with domestics removed
finding: Domestic reporters are the more active observers, and exclusion changes the effort denominator almost uniformly

question: Do single-species specialists distort effort?
what_it_does: Observers with 10+ mammal records where one species exceeds 80% of them
finding: Real but concentrated on backyard squirrels and cats; removing every specialist barely moves the focal species

question: Does spatial clustering of records matter?
what_it_does: Per-cell record caps and their effect on the species-to-effort ratio
finding: Capping moves the ratio the wrong way, so no thinning is applied

question: Should repeat camera locations be grouped?
what_it_does: Variance in deployment year between versus within physical camera locations
finding: 97.8% of the year contrast is between locations; only 1,862 locations were sampled in more than one year

question: Does within-block effort vary?
what_it_does: Busiest-to-quietest effort ratio among 50 km cells inside each 100 km block
finding: Large, but it does not survive controlling for range size, while range size survives controlling for it

question: How much data does a trend need?
what_it_does: Camera and iNaturalist volume crossed on the ecoregion model, 4x4 grid
finding: WITHDRAWN. The regional trend term enters only the iNaturalist likelihood in the model that generated these data, so the simulated camera data carried no regional trend and the 3:1 ratio restates the model structure

question: What power do we have?
what_it_does: Detection rate and false-positive rate by estimator arm and abundance level
finding: 17% power for a sparse species, 40% intermediate, 67% deer-like, with false positives at or near the nominal 5%

question: Is the reported parameter validated?
what_it_does: Bias and coverage of the camera-anchored coefficient rather than the summed trend
finding: Never scored; every run scored the summed parameter and re-scoring from saved output is impossible

question: Can cameras identify a regional trend?
what_it_does: Fork the regional model so the regional deviation enters the camera likelihood too, with an iNaturalist-only regional sink; validate against null, real, spurious and both
finding: Not yet run
